citations.title: Security — Every Action Passes Through Policy First | Naïve
excerpts: # Secure by design. Built for trust.

Your data is stored with established third-party infrastructure providers that maintain industry security and privacy standards. A list of subprocessors and provider attestations is available upon request at [support@usenaive.ai](mailto:support@usenaive.ai) .
## Control your agent's autonomy, protect your business data, and scale with the same rigor as your enterprise stack.
### Your data is not used to train models
We do not use your proprietary business data, prompts, or agent memory to train our foundational models. Your company's intellectual property stays yours.
You decide the level of autonomy. Set strict guardrails, require explicit human approval for sensitive actions (like spending money or publishing), and review agent drafts before they go live.
When you connect third-party apps (Stripe, Meta, LinkedIn), your API keys and OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest and scoped to specific agent workflows. They are never exposed in plaintext.
Your company workspace, agent context, and customer data are logically separated. Strict tenant boundaries ensure your data is never accessible to other organizations.

Hosted on established cloud and data providers that maintain industry security and privacy standards, with encryption in transit and at rest. Subprocessor details available upon request at support@usenaive.ai.
Role-based access controls (RBAC) allow you to dictate who in your organization can view, edit, or approve agent workflows, enforcing least-privilege access.
### Is my data used to train AI models?
No. We do not use your proprietary business data, prompts, or agent memory to train our foundational models. Your work stays your work.
### How are my connected accounts and API keys secured?
Secrets and API credentials are encrypted at rest and scoped to specific agent workflows. They are not exposed in plaintext in logs or interfaces, and access is limited to authorized actions.
### Can agents take actions without my permission?
You are in full control. You can set agents to run fully autonomously, or require human approval for specific actions like publishing a post, sending an email campaign, or spending budget.
### Is Naïve multi-tenant, and how is customer data isolated?
Naïve is a multi-tenant platform with strict logical isolation between workspaces. Your company's data, agent memory, and workflows are not accessible across accounts.

basis.reasoning: The full first-party security page discusses security practices and says provider attestations are available upon request, but names none of SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, or PCI DSS as a claimed certification.

citations.title: Naïve: Autonomous Company Infrastructure | Y Combinator
excerpts: Naïve is an autonomous company runtime.
You describe your business — or connect your existing one — and Naïve deploys AI employees that actually execute.
1. Our employees have their own identity. Own bank account, own email, own credentials, own compute.
2. They sign up for tools, pay for services, deploy apps, and file documents as themselves. No human in the loop.
3. They learn recursively. Every output, every result gets stored. They extract patterns about YOUR business and compound performance week over week.
**New companies** — describe what you want, Naïve builds and runs it.
**Existing companies** — one-click connect your stack (CRM, codebase, Shopify, Notion, whatever), Naïve employees plug in day one.

excerpts: OpenRouter-backed LLM routing — chat completions across 300+ models through one Naive endpoint, billed in credits. Use Naive as a full wrapper over OpenRouter.

The `llm` primitive is a full wrapper over [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/) . It gives your agent a single, OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint that routes to **300+ models** across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, and more — with provider routing, fallbacks, and streaming. You don’t manage an OpenRouter account or key: Naive holds the key and bills each call in **Naive credits** based on the exact cost OpenRouter returns. There are two ways to use it:

citations.title: Naive docs
excerpts: > The most efficient managed agent for long-horizon work. The highest intelligence per dollar, by design.

**Naive Managed Agents is a managed agent platform**: you define an [agent](https://vetta.sh/docs/capabilities/agent.md) — model, prompt, tools, skills, budget — and run it as [sessions](https://vetta.sh/docs/concepts/sessions.md) that work for hours, pause at storage cost, and finish without a person in the loop. You pay per finished task, in real dollars, priced before each call runs.

> **Two layers, one stack.** Naive Managed Agents is the autonomous-company infrastructure — the harness, the managed runtime, sessions, budgets, tools. Naive **blueprints** are the layer on top: the templates a whole company is installed from, and the [studio](https://app.usenaive.ai) you run it in. These pages are the Managed Agents reference; the API, SDK and CLI still identify it as `vetta` (`api.vetta.sh`, `@usenaive-sdk/vetta`, the `vetta` binary).

Everything is built around one number: **the most intelligence per dollar spent** — the same model on different stacks varies several-fold in cost per completed task ([benchmarks](https://usenaive.ai/blogs/introducing-naive-managed-agents)).

![Naive Managed Agents — managed agents infrastructure: any model and provider, skills, and tools in; harness, runtime, orchestration, and self-improvement inside; run and interact through the Web Studio, API, CLI, and SDK](https://mintcdn.com/vetta/Lby8hzUEjDwI2o6a/images/architecture-overview.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Lby8hzUEjDwI2o6a\&q=85\&s=9698e189bb8189f7fdcbdda775751c1f)

Any model, your skills, and your tools go in; Managed Agents' runtime does the work; and you run and interact through the [Web Studio](https://app.usenaive.ai), the [API](https://vetta.sh/docs/api/overview.md), the [CLI](https://vetta.sh/docs/cli/overview.md), or the [SDK](https://vetta.sh/docs/sdk/typescript.md).
## Create an agent, run a session
Everything you touch maps to primitives you create and version — familiar on day one.
> A reusable, versioned config: model, harness, prompt, tools, skills, budget.
> One directly-controlled run of an agent — send input, stream output, interrupt, resume.
> A resumable stream of everything the agent does, keyed by sequence number.
> A disposable sandbox with a filesystem, shell, and optional browser — paused when idle.
> Persisted, versioned expertise loaded with progressive disclosure.
> Durable, organization-scoped storage for the artifacts a session produces.

basis.reasoning: The public Naïve docs portal includes an agent/session reference and multiple linked API, SDK, CLI, capability, and concepts documentation pages.
